title: Compact performance claim ledger and expiry policy for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a compact, signed "performance claim" ledger record and an automated expiry/decay policy to reduce profile churn and provide a lightweight canonical assertion for model onboarding and pinning. The ledger entry is intended to be a machine-consumable, size-bounded artifact that summarizes verified cost/latency/throughput anchors plus provenance (signed by the verification pipeline). This ticket defines schema, TTL semantics, publish/refresh automation, and how the ledger interacts with model pinning, rollback, and the Console UI.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact JSON schema (<= 8KB) for performance claims that includes: model id, model version, normalized latency/throughput/cost anchors, signature metadata, verification timestamp, and expiry/decay parameters
Implement a signature format and storage location for claims (signed by the verification pipeline) and an API to retrieve the latest non-expired claim for a model version
Create a publish workflow in the verification pipeline that emits claim ledger entries after successful perf verification with an expiry TTL and optional decay curve
Console shows claim status (fresh/stale/expired) on the model profile page and surfaces the signed claim with a link to the verification run and perf artifacts
Pinning logic prefers a non-expired claim; if claim is expired, pinning UI warns and provides options to re-run verification or force-pin with justification
Automated refresh job runs sampled production shadowing to trigger claim re-issuance for high-impact models before expiry
Telemetry emits claim age, frequency of refreshes, and a count of models with expired claims; alerts fire if >15% of enterprise customer pinned models have expired claims
End-to-end tests and a simulation harness validate claim expiry handling under clock skew and delayed verification runs
implementation_notes: Backend: Add 'claims' table (or S3-backed objects) with enforced max payload size; each claim carries signature metadata and 'expiry_ts' and 'decay_profile' fields
Verification pipeline change: after profile validation, produce signed compact claim and push to claims store; include link to full perf artifacts for debugging
API: GET /models/{id}/claims?include_expired=false returns latest non-expired claim; add header X-Claim-Age and X-Claim-Signature
Console: Model profile gets a compact claim card with status badge and action buttons (Re-verify, Force Pin, View Verification Run)
Pinning/Runtime: Router considers claim freshness when offering pinned defaults and exposes fallback behavior if claim expired (e.g., route to compatible variant)
Ops: Scheduled job: refresh-candidate-selector selects top N models by traffic and claims-before-expiry to prioritize refresh runs
Security: Keep signing keys in KMS/HSM; rotate keys with versioned signatures and provide verification helpers in SDKs
